items.title: Public underscore-prefixed fields convention (context._device, _adapter, _ssrCache)
items.claim: Underscore-prefixed public fields are a deliberate convention that lets external code write to them without compiler complaint.
items.evidence: packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:490-491 (`public _adapter`, `public _device`), :1098 names it 'the same convention as `public _device` and `public _canvas`'; WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:220 (`public _pipelineCache`) and the Q35 culler-pool slice flipped 14 more fields to it. No row questions the convention.
items.migrate_text: The WebGPU renderer uses public underscore-prefixed fields as its cross-module access convention (WebGPUContext.ts:490-491 `public _adapter` / `public _device`; the comment at :1098 names it). TypeScript therefore cannot stop external code writing to `_device`, `_adapter` or a renderer's `_pipelineCache`; the convention is deliberate and documented, not a defect, but the new review should state it once so readers do not mistake it for leaked encapsulation.

items.title: Same-file diagnostic latches (_execDebugLogged, _globePassRPLogged, _diagTileCount, _postInitDebugLogged ...) with no shared throttle
items.claim: Per-instance `_xxxLogged` booleans concentrated in WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts and WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts are extra state nobody resets; pragma-stripped so zero runtime cost, but a code-reading cost.
items.evidence: WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1079 `_execDebugLogged`, :1081 `_postInitDebugLogged`, :1088 `_globePassRPLogged`; nine distinct `_...Logged` fields across the two files, 22 `Logged` references in SceneRenderer alone; one `_diagLastLogTime` site. No LogThrottle / DiagnosticThrottle helper exists anywhere under packages/engine/Source/Renderer. Same item as T9 and N5; no queue row.
items.migrate_text: Diagnostic one-shot logging is still implemented as ad-hoc per-instance latches: WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:1079-1088 declares `_execDebugLogged`, `_postInitDebugLogged` and `_globePassRPLogged`, nine distinct `_...Logged` fields exist across WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts and WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts, and a single `_diagLastLogTime` throttle is hand-rolled. They are pragma-stripped (zero production cost) but nothing resets them and no shared helper exists; the pragma-stripped predicate pattern in CLAUDE.md ('Logging & Debug Pragmas') is the shape a centralised helper should take. Low severity; readability only.

items.title: Failure mode: device lost - recovery exists; per-object caches (C-R12-PER-OBJECT-CACHES) not on the cache-clear walk
items.claim: WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery handles backoff/3 attempts/3-state machine; per-object `_webgpuCache` owners are not cleared on recovery and rely on next-frame churn.
items.evidence: Recovery: WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery.ts (744 lines) still has HEALTHY/RECOVERING/FATAL (:27-31), maxAttempts default 3 (:240), dispose race handling (:448), and a unit spec (packages/engine/Specs/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUDeviceLossRecoverySpec.js, Batch 660, ten cases). Per-object walk: Batch 197 added `clearPerObjectCaches(scene)` (WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:233, :604) and Batch 778 fixed Point/Label teardown, but DEFERRED_WORK.md:8360-8380 (C-R12-PER-OBJECT-CACHES, PARTIAL, 2026-07-31 correction) and QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md:1639/:2452 (`C11-20`, PARTIAL) keep the nested/tileset-owned/`_webgpuLabelCache`/device-loss walk OPEN. Q-65 (render loop stopping after recovery) is CLOSED Edge-confirmed (FIX_QUEUE:860); FAR-208 is active with 'focused physical-browser recovery suite' remaining.
items.migrate_text: Device-loss recovery is real: WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery.ts keeps the HEALTHY/RECOVERING/FATAL machine (:27-31), three attempts with exponential backoff (:240), dispose-during-recovery handling (:448) and a ten-case unit spec (WebGPUDeviceLossRecoverySpec.js); Q-65 proved the post-recovery render loop survives in Edge. What remains is the per-object cache walk: `clearPerObjectCaches` (WebGPUSceneRendererEnsureResources.ts:604, called at :233) only reaches owners exposing a literal `_webgpuCache`, so tileset-owned/nested model caches, clipping caches and non-literal fields such as `_webgpuLabelCache` are still not invalidated on a replacement device - row `C11-20` / C-R12-PER-OBJECT-CACHES (PARTIAL, Batch 778) and FAR-208's remaining physical-browser recovery suite own it.

items.title: Failure mode: OOM - no pushErrorScope('out-of-memory'), no memory-pressure callback
items.claim: Only validation error scopes exist; a real OOM surfaces as device loss; no app-side graceful-degrade hook.
items.evidence: `grep pushErrorScope` over packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU finds 12 scopes, all `"validation"` (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2271, WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders.ts:273/376, WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550/3676/3748/3819, WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:2125, WebGPUPrimitiveIndexUtils.ts:56, WebGPURenderBundleManager.ts:402); zero `out-of-memory` scopes; no `uncapturederror` listener. The per-frame allocation storm behind BUG-9 is addressed by WebGPURingBufferAllocator.ts (used by WebGPUContext.ts and WebGPUModelCameraArena.ts). FORK_ARCHITECTURE_REMEDIATION_PLAN_2026-07-13.md:205 states 'Runtime OOM or device loss enters recovery' as a principle but no queue row tracks OOM scoping or a memory-pressure callback.
items.migrate_text: The renderer never pushes an `out-of-memory` error scope: all 12 `pushErrorScope` sites under packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU are `"validation"` scopes (e.g. WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2271, WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550, WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:2125) and no `uncapturederror` listener exists, so a texture or buffer allocation that fails for memory is only observed when it escalates to device loss and takes the WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery path. There is also no memory-pressure hook by which an application can degrade LOD or drop effects before that point. The FAR plan (:205) states the intent that runtime OOM enters recovery cleanly, but no row funds OOM-scoped allocation or a pressure callback.

items.title: Failure mode: shader compile failure - logged with context ID, no auto-fallback placeholder shader
items.claim: Compile errors are logged with context id; a compile failure on a hot-path shader yields a render hole.
items.evidence: Logging: WebGPUContext.ts:3496-3506 wraps `createShaderModule` and reports `getCompilationInfo()` errors as `[CesiumJS:webgpu:<ctx>] Shader ... compilation ERROR` (permanent console.error); WebGPUShaderModule.ts no longer has its own console.error sites (0). Fallback: Batch 388 (2a85a37112, C2-22) added the flat-magenta ErrorPipeline.wgsl substituted by WebGPUModelPipelineCache when a model PBR pipeline fails validation - model path only. Other renderers' shader failures still produce holes. Same residual as F4/T7/N4.
items.surviving_record: Batch 388 (model PBR only); residual has no row
items.migrate_text: Shader compile errors are surfaced with the context id by the `createShaderModule` hook at WebGPUContext.ts:3496-3506, and a failed model PBR pipeline now draws flat magenta via Shaders/WebGPU/Model/ErrorPipeline.wgsl (WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550-3819 validation scopes, Batch 388). Every other renderer - globe (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders.ts:273/376), primitives, post-process stages, render bundles - still logs and then silently drops the draw, so a hot-path shader regression outside the model path is a render hole with a console line and nothing on screen.

items.title: Failure mode: pipeline create failure - validation scopes at three sites; only f16->f32 auto-fallback
items.claim: Three pushErrorScope('validation') sites; the tonemapping f16->f32 path is the only auto-fallback.
items.evidence: Validation scopes now at nine non-scene sites (listed under F2). Auto-fallbacks today: f16->f32 stage recompile in WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts ~2110-2150 (`fallbackWgslCode`) and the Batch 388 magenta ErrorPipeline for model PBR. FIX_QUEUE_2026-08-27_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md:1394 (fleet1 LOW PLAUSIBLE, QUEUED) additionally flags WebGPURenderBundleManager.ts:402-419 leaking its validation scope when the record callback throws. No generic 'known-good pipeline variant' fallback exists.
items.surviving_record: Batch 388 + FIX_QUEUE fleet1 row at :1394 (bundle scope leak)
items.migrate_text: Pipeline creation is guarded by validation error scopes in nine places (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders.ts:273/376, WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550/3676/3748/3819, WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:2125, WebGPUPrimitiveIndexUtils.ts:56, WebGPURenderBundleManager.ts:402), but only two produce a substitute: the f16->f32 recompile in WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts (~2110-2150, `fallbackWgslCode`) and the magenta model ErrorPipeline (Batch 388). A failed globe, primitive, collection or bundle pipeline is logged and its draws vanish. The bundle site is also queued as a scope leak (FIX_QUEUE fleet1 row at :1394): `_recordBundleWithValidation` has no try/finally around the caller's record callback.

items.title: Failure mode: lost canvas (tab background, monitor disconnect) - no explicit visibilitychange handler
items.claim: Same path as device loss on Chromium; no visibilitychange handler; mostly moot.
items.evidence: `visibilitychange` appears only in packages/engine/Source/Scene/FrameRateMonitor.js:115-121 (upstream FPS monitor); nothing under Renderer/ listens. `WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery._reconfigureCanvas` path still exists via the DeviceLossRecoveryHost interface (WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery.ts:90 region) and WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts owns swap-chain configuration. No row; the audit itself rated it moot.
items.migrate_text: No renderer code reacts to `visibilitychange`; the only listener is upstream's FrameRateMonitor.js:115-121. Swap-chain reconfiguration after a backgrounded tab or monitor change rides the device-loss host path (WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery.ts host interface, WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts) exactly as in 2026-04. Chromium drops and restores the swap-chain silently, so this stays a low-severity observation rather than a defect.

items.title: Failure mode: WebGPU not available - renderer:'webgpu' did not auto-fall-back when requestAdapter returned null
items.claim: Only `navigator.gpu` presence is checked at the factory; explicit `renderer:'webgpu'` throws instead of falling back when the adapter is null at runtime.
items.evidence: Batch 667 (9ac30e54e2, SOL-LAND-12, ratified 2026-07-16) rebuilt ContextFactory around `getRendererAttemptPlan`: packages/engine/Source/Renderer/ContextFactory.ts:231-300 iterates an attempt plan, an explicitly requested WebGPU that fails at any stage (availability/adapter/device) falls back to WebGL with a permanent `console.warn` and structured `diagnostics`, and `strictRenderer: true` removes the fallback. WebGPUDevicePool.ts:792-799 wraps `requestAdapter` failures into a stage-tagged RendererInitializationError. FAR-102 ('renderer selection centralized ... transactional') is the ledger record.
items.migrate_text: Resolved at Batch 667 (ContextFactory attempt plan + strictRenderer); FAR-102 records it.

items.title: Failure mode: GPU validation errors after init are silent - the per-frame validation scope is one-shot
items.claim: The globe-pass validation scope fires on the first frame only; a mid-session regression (e.g. HDR toggle without bumping `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration`) is silent until reload.
items.evidence: WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2268-2286: `if (device && !this._globeValidationDone) { this._globeValidationDone = true; device.pushErrorScope("validation"); ... }` - unchanged one-shot. No `uncapturederror` listener anywhere in Renderer/WebGPU (grep = 0) and no `frameState.debug`-gated per-pass scope. Same item as N6; no queue row (Q-65/Q-135 cover device loss, not validation).
items.migrate_text: Post-init GPU validation errors are still only caught on the first globe pass: WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2268-2286 pushes a single `"validation"` scope guarded by `_globeValidationDone` and never again, and the renderer registers no `device.onuncapturederror` / `uncapturederror` listener (zero hits under Renderer/WebGPU). A format or layout regression introduced mid-session - an HDR toggle that misses a `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` reader, a new pipeline variant - produces browser-console noise the engine never sees and no probe can assert. A permanent `uncapturederror` handler that stamps the context id, plus an optional debug-mode per-pass scope, would close it cheaply.

items.title: Failure mode: SSR samples an uninitialized normal placeholder with no warning (FEAT-GAP-01 normal G-buffer)
items.claim: WebGPUSceneRenderer passes `undefined` for the normal view; SSR ships noise, not reflections, and stays silent.
items.evidence: Warning: Batch 117 (0bcc65689c) added the one-shot pragma-wrapped warning at WebGPUSSREffect.ts:212-223 and the `normalTextureView ? 1 : 0` uniform (:273). G-buffer: Phase 8a landed (WebGPUGBufferRenderer.ts, `scene.deferredLighting` at Scene.js:1159-1166, `view.gBufferFramebuffer` allocated on every non-pick WebGPU frame per WebGPUContext.ts:5127-5138) and WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.ts:200-201 now hands `view.gBufferFramebuffer.normalRoughnessTexture` to `executeSSR` (:311). Residual: the compute normal producer runs only when `frameState.useDeferredLighting` is true (WebGPUContext.ts:5127-5137; WebGPUGBufferRenderer.ts docstring), and SSR does not demand it, so at defaults the attachment holds the clear sentinel wherever a pipeline lacks a normal-roughness output. FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:881 still says 'gated on FEAT-GAP-01 normal G-buffer for full fidelity' (stale wording).
items.surviving_record: Batch 117 (warning) + Phase 8a G-buffer; residual has no row; FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:881
items.migrate_text: SSR is no longer silent and no longer structurally starved: WebGPUSSREffect.ts:212-223 warns once when no normal view arrives, and WebGPUSceneRendererEnvironmentalEffects.ts:200-201/311 feeds it `view.gBufferFramebuffer.normalRoughnessTexture`, which WebGPUContext.ts:5127-5138 allocates on every non-pick frame. The remaining gap is demand: the depth-derived normal producer (WebGPUGBufferRenderer.ts) dispatches only under `scene.deferredLighting` (Scene.js:1159-1166), and `scene.screenSpaceReflections` does not raise that demand, so with defaults SSR marches against an attachment that is the clear sentinel for every pipeline without a normal-roughness output. Either SSR should demand the producer or the docs (FEATURE_INVENTORY.md:881 still cites FEAT-GAP-01) should say that `deferredLighting` is the switch.

items.title: Failure mode: indirect-draw / index-buffer overflow guards are recommended, not enforced
items.claim: CLAUDE.md says new subsystems SHOULD add re-entry / null-target / size guards; some renderers do, some don't; nothing enforces it.
items.evidence: CLAUDE.md 'Permanent sentinels to add for new subsystems' is unchanged ('SHOULD'). Tools/lint-debug-pragmas.mjs enforces console-pragma wrapping only; ci-guards.spec.mjs and pre-push-guard.mjs do not check sentinels. WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts still carries first-frame diagnostics (:1079-1088) and a null-FB console.error; no lint or type-level check covers other renderers. No row.
items.migrate_text: The three permanent sentinels CLAUDE.md asks of every subsystem (re-entry counter, null render-target guard, buffer-size validation before submit) remain a SHOULD with no mechanical check: Tools/lint-debug-pragmas.mjs only polices console pragmas, and neither ci-guards.spec.mjs nor pre-push-guard.mjs inspects renderer sources. Coverage is therefore uneven across the 276 files under Renderer/WebGPU and a new renderer can land without any of them. A census in the new review (which renderers have which sentinel) is the cheapest next step.

items.title: Embeddability: multi-instance safety strong (ContextRegistry per-guid ids, DevicePool refcount 'Strategy B')
items.claim: Per-context guid ids; one GPUDevice ref-counted across canvases; released when refCount hits 0.
items.evidence: ContextRegistry is still static on GraphicsContext; WebGPUDevicePool.ts:76-77 (`destroyed only when refCount hits zero`, `releaseDevice`), :285 `refCount`, and :20-21/:459-482 add the feature-level compatibility check on sharing. FAR-102/103 (renderer selection + FeatureRenderer readiness transactional) are active with 'long-running multi-context/device-loss soak' remaining.
items.migrate_text: Multi-instance embedding still rests on GraphicsContext's static ContextRegistry of guid-keyed contexts and on WebGPUDevicePool ref-counting one GPUDevice across canvases (WebGPUDevicePool.ts:285 `refCount`, :76-77 release-to-zero destroys), now with a core-vs-compatibility feature-level check before a device is shared (:459-482). FAR-102/103 made selection and FeatureRenderer readiness transactional; the long multi-context/device-loss soak they list as remaining is still the open proof.

items.title: Embeddability: global state pollution minimal (one `globalScope.__skyAtmoDiagLogged` debug latch)
items.claim: Only one real globalThis write in the WebGPU directory, a once-per-tab debug latch.
items.evidence: Non-comment `globalThis`/`globalScope` writes today: WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js:990 `__skyAtmoDiagLogged`, :1009 `__skyAtmoDiagPushLogged`, :1237 `__skyAtmoDiagFinalLogged` - all inside `//>>includeStart('debug')` blocks (:984). WebGPUCpuPassProfiler.ts:622-623 `window.head` is a local variable named `window`, not the global. So the pollution grew from one latch to three, all debug-stripped.
items.migrate_text: Global-scope writes from the WebGPU renderer are still confined to sky-atmosphere debug latches, now three of them (`globalScope.__skyAtmoDiagLogged` / `__skyAtmoDiagPushLogged` / `__skyAtmoDiagFinalLogged` at WebGPUSkyAtmosphereRenderer.js:990, :1009, :1237), every one inside a pragma-stripped block. Nothing else under Renderer/WebGPU assigns to `globalThis` or `window` (the `window.head` at WebGPUCpuPassProfiler.ts:622 is a local named `window`). Embedders get a clean global namespace in production builds.

items.title: Embeddability: `_globalDefaultRenderer` single process-wide default; mixed-backend apps relying on it behave unpredictably
items.claim: One shared module variable set by variant entry barrels; risk if apps omit `contextOptions.renderer`.
items.evidence: The singleton still exists (RendererType.ts:263 `let _globalDefaultRenderer = RendererType.WEBGPU`, setter :269, getter :277) but NO caller invokes `setGlobalDefaultRenderer(` anywhere in packages/engine/Source, packages/widgets/Source, scripts/ or the generated Source/Cesium*.js barrels (grep = 0; the barrels only re-export it). Variant defaults now come from build-time aliased `rendererBuildCapabilities` (scripts/stubs/rendererBuildCapabilitiesWebGL.js / WebGPU.js) consumed by `getDefaultRendererType(preferWebGPU, buildCapabilities)` (RendererType.ts ~291) and ContextFactory. BUILD_AND_VARIANTS.md:231-237 documents the setter as module-level with no effect on explicit `renderer`.
items.migrate_text: Stale premise: no barrel or engine code calls `setGlobalDefaultRenderer`; variant defaults flow through build-aliased `rendererBuildCapabilities`.

items.title: Browser portability: Chromium first-class; no Firefox CI; no Safari coverage or Safari-specific workarounds
items.claim: Visual regression runs Edge only; Playwright Firefox is Nightly without WebGPU; nothing references Safari/WebKit.
items.evidence: Tooling now accepts other engines: Tools/visual-regression/capture-and-diff.mjs:692-695 (`--browser firefox|webkit` -> playwright.firefox/webkit) and Tools/variant-smoke-test.mjs:186 (`--browser msedge|chromium|firefox|webkit`). But scripts/karmaDefaultBrowsers.js resolves only ChromeDebugging/EdgeCompat/Chrome, no scheduled Firefox/WebKit run exists, and DEFERRED_WORK.md:4850-4855 (NEW-CI-GPU-GLOBALS-HOST-GUARD shipped Batch 243; NEW-CI-COVERAGE-SUITE 'unknown until next hosted run' under FirefoxHeadless) is the only Firefox record. Safari/WebKit still appears only in comments (WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts:83, WebGPUImageUpload.ts:18/226); no UA sniffing (good). Same as T8/N7.
items.surviving_record: DEFERRED_WORK.md NEW-CI-COVERAGE-SUITE (:4855); tooling flags in capture-and-diff.mjs / variant-smoke-test.mjs
items.migrate_text: Cross-browser coverage is still Edge-only in practice: capture-and-diff.mjs:692-695 and variant-smoke-test.mjs:186 can launch Playwright Firefox or WebKit, but no scheduled or banked run uses them, scripts/karmaDefaultBrowsers.js only resolves Chrome/Edge, and DEFERRED_WORK.md:4855 (NEW-CI-COVERAGE-SUITE) records the last Firefox attempt as 'unknown until next hosted run'. The renderer contains no Safari or WebKit workaround and no user-agent sniffing (the only mentions are comments at WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts:83 and WebGPUImageUpload.ts:18/226). A Firefox-release + Safari Technology Preview smoke leg, even weekly and manual, remains the recommendation; it needs an owner row.

items.title: Feature detection: `useHardwareClipDistances` / `useShaderF16` opt-in even when granted; no userAgent sniffing
items.claim: Runtime feature flags update from the enabled-feature set; the two risky features stay opt-in; no UA sniffing.
items.evidence: WebGPUContext.ts:997 `public useHardwareClipDistances = false`, :1014 `public useShaderF16 = false`, :3603-3604 opt-in comment, :7018-7019 snapshot. No `userAgent` reference under Renderer/WebGPU. WebGPUDevicePool.ts:512 performs the `features.has(f)` probe.
items.migrate_text: Optional-feature posture is unchanged and correct: `useHardwareClipDistances` and `useShaderF16` default to false (WebGPUContext.ts:997, :1014) and must be opted into even when the adapter grants the feature, WebGPUDevicePool.ts:512 gates on `features.has(...)`, and nothing under Renderer/WebGPU sniffs `userAgent`. The new review can carry this as a one-line strength.

items.title: Top-10 #10: `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` invalidation contract is manual (23 files); no compile-time check that a new renderer reads it
items.claim: One missed reader = stale pipeline + format-mismatch validation warning.
items.evidence: Definition at WebGPUContext.ts:922 (`public _scenePipelineFormatGeneration = 0`, getter :942); 31 files under packages/engine/Source now reference it (up from 23). No `recompileForSceneFormat` method or `FormatAwareRenderer` interface exists (grep = 0). Same as N8. No queue row; FAR Phase 6 ('Complete generation invalidation/teardown', :302) is the nearest umbrella but names device generation, not the scene format generation.
items.migrate_text: The scene pipeline format contract is still convention-only: `WebGPUContext._scenePipelineFormatGeneration` (WebGPUContext.ts:922, getter :942) is read by 31 files, each of which must remember to compare its cached generation and rebuild, and nothing at compile time or lint time says which renderers are format-aware. A renderer that forgets keeps a pipeline whose color/depth format no longer matches the scene target after an HDR or MSAA change, and (per F7) the resulting validation error is not even caught after the first frame. Declaring a `recompileForSceneFormat(generation)` method on a shared interface that every feature renderer implements would make the contract greppable and compiler-checked.
